src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Bharat Petroleum – 'Energising lives'; Indian Oil – 'The energy of India'; the other two taglines as per the printed key.

s: Where is Naharkatiya oil field located?
x: Naharkatiya oil field is in upper Assam (Brahmaputra valley).

s: In which place, the oldest refinery of India is located?
x: Digboi (Assam, 1901) is India's oldest refinery; Noonmati came in 1962.

s: In a well, oil, air and water (from bottom to top) are arranged in which ascending order?
x: Fluids settle by density in a trap: water at the bottom, then oil, then gas/air on top.

s: The Naharkatiya oil field is located at a distance of 32 km:
x: Naharkatiya oil field lies about 32 km south-west of Digboi.

s: Where is Tatipaka oil refinery located?
x: Tatipaka is an ONGC mini refinery in Konaseema, Andhra Pradesh.

s: The largest petroleum reserves are found in :
x: Of the options Saudi Arabia has the largest oil reserves; Venezuela (not offered) is now first.

s: Which one of the following is not correctly matched? Oil Refineries Set up by
x: Bina (BPCL), Tatipaka (ONGC) and Digboi (IOCL) are correctly matched; Koyali is an IOCL refinery, so its printed pairing is wrong. The option text lost the companies.

s: Which one of the following countries has the largest known reserves of oil :
x: Iran (157.8 bn barrels) has more oil reserves than Iraq (145), Kuwait (101.5) or Nigeria.

s: Tatipaka Oil Refinery is located in the state of –
x: Tatipaka refinery is in Andhra Pradesh (ONGC).

s: To insulate the country from disruptions in the supply of crude oil, India has established "India Strategic Petroleum Reserves Ltd." It will construct underground storages at three places. Identify the place which has not been selected for the purpose.
x: The SPRs are at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur; Ankleshwar was not selected.

s: Which one of the following facts about Bombay High Oil Field is not correct?
o: Bombay High Oil Field lies 60 km off Mumbai coast
The first oil well was drilled in 1974
It was discovered jointly by Russian and Indian teams
x:
Most books and keys: (a). Strictly, the 'discovered in 1965' statement is also loose – the Indian-Russian seismic survey was in 1964-65, oil was struck in 1974 (PMF) and NCERT dates the discovery to 1973.
Bombay High lies about 160 km, not 60 km, off Mumbai, so statement (a) is wrong.

s: KG-D6 Basin, which has been in the news since April, 2009 has large reserves of :
x: KG-D6 off Andhra Pradesh is a natural-gas block.

s: Most of the production of natural gas in India comes from :
x: Mumbai High (western offshore) gives most of India's natural gas; offshore areas produce about 64%.

s: Where was the first oil well drilled in India?
x: The first oil well was drilled at Makum, upper Assam, in 1867; Digboi was the first commercial find.

s: Which country has the largest reserves of oil?
x: Venezuela has the world's largest proven oil reserves (303.8 bn barrels).

s: Which one amongst the following is the oldest refinery in India?
x: Digboi (1901) is the oldest refinery; Koyali 1965, Haldia 1975, Mathura 1982.

s: The oil exploration in India is undertaken by –
x: Oil India Ltd (with ONGC) explores for oil; HPCL and IOC refine and market.

s: Ankleshwar is famous for –
x: Ankleshwar (Bharuch, Gujarat) is an oil field.

s: Where is no oil refinery mentioned below?
x: Hatia (Jharkhand) has no refinery; Koyali, Noonmati and Barauni do.

s: In which of the following state of India 'Koyali' petroleum refinery is located?
x: Koyali refinery (IOCL) is near Vadodara, Gujarat.

s: The Noonmati oil refinery is located in the state of
x: Noonmati (Guwahati) refinery is in Assam.

s:
Which of the following is true about petroleum production?

I. 60% of the world’s petroleum deposits are found in the middle East.

II. Petroleum reserve in Alaska is certified equivalent to Texas.

III. USA is a prominent producer and importer for petroleum.
Codes
x: The Middle East holds well over half of world oil reserves, Alaska is a major US oil area and the USA is both a big producer and importer, so all are taken as true.

s: Which one of the following sequences of the oil refineries of India, as they occur from South to North, is correct?
x: South to north on the west coast: Kochi (Kerala), Mangalore (Karnataka), Mumbai, Koyali (Gujarat).

s: The oldest oil field in India is
x: Digboi (Assam) is India's oldest oil field, producing from 1889.

s: To insulate the country from disruptions in supply of crude oil, India has established “India Strategic Petroleum Reserves ltd.” It will construct underground storages at three places. Identify the place which has not been selected for the purpose.
x: India's SPRs are at Padur, Visakhapatnam and Mangaluru; Ankleshwar was not selected.

s:
Consider the following statements.

I. Petronet LNG Ltd is setting up another LNG terminal at Mangalore.

II. The Head Office of the Dredging Corporation of India is at Visakhapatnam.

III. The Narwapahar Mine is operated by the Uranium Corporation of India Limited.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Dredging Corporation's head office is at Visakhapatnam and UCIL operates the Narwapahar uranium mine; statement 1 is taken as true per the key.

s:
Consider the following oil fields of India:

I. Digboi

II. Moran

III. Kalol

IV. Naharkatiya
Which of the above oil fields are located in Assam?
x: Digboi, Moran and Naharkatiya are Assam oilfields; Kalol is in Gujarat.

s: In which of the following countries mineral oil was commercially drilled in 1857 ?
x: Romania was the first country with officially recorded commercial oil output (1857).

s: Which is the biggest refinery in India?
x: Jamnagar (Reliance, Gujarat) is India's biggest refinery and the world's largest refining complex.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
s: In 2020, which country discovered that shallow natural gas reserves contain about 80 trillion cubic feet of natural gas?
x: In February 2020 the UAE announced a shallow gas field between Abu Dhabi and Dubai (Jebel Ali) with about 80 trillion cubic feet of gas.

s: Navgam oil field is located in –
x: Navgam, like Ankleshwar, Kalol and Mehsana, is an oil field of Gujarat. Moved (energy).

s: The ONGC's supply ship that drowned in the Arabian Sea recently was:
x: The SICAL-operated ONGC supply vessel Samudrika-10 sank off Mumbai (Bombay High, Arabian Sea) on 9 July 2007. Off-topic news item, moved.

src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
s: Which of the following is an example of renewable energy used in the energy transition?
x: Solar and wind are renewable and are the energy-transition sources; coal, diesel and nuclear fission use finite fuels.

src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
s: Fuel used in thermal power plant is
x: Thermal power plants burn fossil fuels, mainly coal (also gas); uranium is used in nuclear plants.

src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
s: Which of the following is not a fossil fuel?
x: Solar energy is a renewable source; coal, natural gas and petroleum are fossil fuels.

src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
s: Which of the following is not a petroleum product?
x: Coal is a fossil fuel mined from rocks, not a product of petroleum refining; kerosene, diesel and petrol are.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s:
There are two statements given below, marked as P and Q.
P: Petroleum and natural gas are fossil fuels.
Q: Coal can be prepared in the laboratory from dead organisms.
Read the above statements and choose the correct option.
o: P is true but Q is false
P is false but Q is true
Both P and Q are true
Both P and Q are false
x: Petroleum and natural gas are fossil fuels (P true); fossil fuels cannot be prepared in a laboratory from dead organisms (Q false).

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
s: Which of the following is not a fossil fuel?
x: Wood is biomass, a renewable fuel, not a fossil fuel; coal, kerosene and natural gas are fossil-derived.

src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer in Sainik Welfare Service
s: Which one of the following is not a non-renewable fuel?
x: Biofuel comes from biomass and is renewable; petroleum, natural gas and coal are non-renewable.

s: Modern environmental technology has enabled us to capture this naturally occurring energy and convert it into electricity or useful heat. Which of the following is NOT a source of renewable energy?
x: Natural gas is a fossil fuel and therefore non-renewable; sunlight, tides and geothermal heat are renewable.

s: The Earth's Sources function for natural resources includes water minerals, fish stocks & ______.
x: The Earth's source function supplies natural resources such as water, minerals, fish stocks and fossil fuels.

s:
In the Union Budget 2011-12, a full exemption from the basic customs duty was extended to the bio-based asphalt (bio asphalt). What is the importance of this material?
1. Unlike traditional asphalt, bio-asphalt is not based on fossil fuels.
2. Bio asphalt can be made from non-renewable resources.
3. Bio asphalt can be made from organic waste materials.
4. It is eco-friendly to use bio asphalt for surfacing of the roads.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Bio-asphalt is made from renewable, organic waste materials rather than fossil fuels and is eco-friendly for roads; statement 2 (non-renewable) is wrong.

s: Which one of the following is not a fossil fuel?
x: Uranium is a non-renewable nuclear fuel, not a fossil fuel; coal, petroleum and natural gas are fossil fuels.

s: An ultimate source of energy stored in fossil fuels is :
x: The energy in fossil fuels came originally from sunlight captured by ancient plants and organisms.

s: A non-renewable source of energy is :
x: Petroleum is a fossil fuel and non-renewable; solar, wind and biogas are renewable.

s: Which is not a renewable resource ?
x: Energy of water (hydro), the Sun (solar) and the Earth (geothermal) are all renewable, so none of them is non-renewable.

s: Which is not a fossil fuel?
x: Wood is biomass, renewable, not a fossil fuel; coal, diesel and petrol are fossil-derived.

s: Which of the following sources of energy is not a commercial source?
x: Biogas is a non-commercial source; petroleum, atomic energy and natural gas are commercial sources.

s: Commercial sources of energy purely consist of-
o: Power, coal, oil, gas, hydro-electricity and uranium
Coal, oil, firewood, vegetable waste and agricultural
Power, coal, animal dung and firewood
x: Commercial energy = power, coal, oil, gas, hydro-electricity and uranium; firewood, dung and farm waste are non-commercial.

s: When did the first oil crisis/energy crisis occur in India?
x: The first oil crisis came in 1973 when OPEC quadrupled oil prices; the second followed in 1979 – the 1970s-80s.

s: Coal, Crude Oil and Natural gas are called –
x: Coal, crude oil and natural gas are fossil fuels, formed over millions of years from buried organisms.

s: Which of the following is an example of fossil fuel?
x: Natural gas is a fossil fuel; wood is biomass, and coke and producer gas are manufactured fuels.

s: Which of the following do not have a major reserve of lignite?
x: Jharkhand has Gondwana coal but no major lignite; Gujarat and Puducherry have lignite, and West Bengal has small lignite resources.

s: Which one of the the following is the largest lignite coal field in India?
x: Neyveli (Tamil Nadu) is the largest lignite field; Singrauli, Makum and Karanpura are coal fields.

s: The Neyveli thermal power plant is fed by :
x: Neyveli is fed by lignite, which is Tertiary coal (15-60 million years), not Gondwana coal.

s: Jharia coalfield is located in which of the following states?
x: Jharia coalfield is in Dhanbad district, Jharkhand.

s: Where was first coal mine in India mined?
x: India's first coal mine was opened at Raniganj (West Bengal) in 1774.

s: Combustion of underground coal occurs in the State of :
x: Underground coal fires burn in the Jharia coalfield of Jharkhand.

s: Which one of the following river valleys is most important in respect of coal reserves of the Gondwana period?
x: The Damodar valley holds the largest and most productive Gondwana coalfields (Jharia, Bokaro, Raniganj).

s: Which of the following river valleys is rich in coal reserves in India?
o: More than one of the above
x: Gondwana coal occurs in the Damodar, Mahanadi, Son and Godavari valleys, so more than one of the options is right.

s:
Assertion (A): Lignite is an inferior variety of coal containing 35-40 percent of carbon.
Reason (R) : Jharkhand is the largest producer of lignite in India. In the context of the above statements, which of the following is true:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
x:
Most books and keys: A true. Strictly, lignite has about 40-55% carbon (PMF Human & Economic Geography 03 p.13; NextGen 40-50%), only Gujarat lignite about 35%.
R is false: Tamil Nadu, not Jharkhand, is the largest lignite producer; A is taken as true (lignite is an inferior, low-carbon coal).

s: In which of the following coal region the coal reserve is maximum?
x:
Most books and keys: Raniganj by total reserves. NCERT calls Jharia the largest coalfield (OnlyIAS NCERT Human Geography 10, Ch7), meaning the richest coking-coal field.
By GSI resource figures Raniganj (about 24,633 MT) holds more coal than Jharia (19,430 MT), Korba or Singrauli.

s: Which State has the largest reserves of Lignite Coal
x: Tamil Nadu holds about 80% of India's lignite reserves (Neyveli).

s: Largest deposit of lignite coal is found in India at –
x: The largest lignite deposits are in Tamil Nadu (Neyveli).

s: In Uttar Pradesh, coal deposits are found in
x: UP's coal lies in the Singrauli region (Sonbhadra), the UP part of the Singrauli coalfield.

s: In which one of the following states are Namchik-Namphuk coal fields located?
x: Namchik-Namphuk is a Tertiary coalfield of Arunachal Pradesh, the eastward extension of the upper Assam coal belt.

s: Which one of the following states of India is the largest producer of lignite coal?
x: Tamil Nadu (Neyveli) is the largest lignite producer, ahead of Gujarat and Rajasthan.

s: The contribution of Chota Nagpur in production of coal, is approx :
x: The Chota Nagpur plateau (Jharkhand, Odisha, WB, Chhattisgarh) gave about 80% of India's coal when the question was set.

s: Bisrampur is famous for the mining of –
x: Bisrampur (Surajpur, Chhattisgarh) is a coalfield.

s: Talcher is a famous coal region, located in :
x: Talcher coalfield is in Angul district, Odisha (Mahanadi Coalfields).

s: Talcher is the famous coal field of :
x: Talcher coalfield is in Odisha.

s:
Which of the following pairs is / are correctly matched ? (Coal Producing Area) (State)
1. Mawlong – Arunachal Pradesh
2. Raniganj – West Bengal
3. Ramgarh – Jharkhand
4. Talcher – Odisha
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
x: Mawlong is in Meghalaya (not Arunachal); Raniganj–WB, Ramgarh–Jharkhand and Talcher–Odisha are right.

s: The main source of energy in India is
x: Thermal power has the largest share of India's installed capacity (48.07%, Dec 2025) and coal gives over 70% of generation.

s: The highest share in power generation in India is of :
x: Thermal power has the highest share in India's power generation; hydro and nuclear are far smaller.

s: The correct sequence of energy sources in order of their share in the power sector in India is :
x:
wind passed nuclear by 2014 and solar and wind have since passed hydro — now Thermal > Solar > Wind > Hydro > Nuclear by capacity (app notes 4:99, Aug 2026 data)
Thermal leads, then hydro; of the orders offered only Thermal > Hydro > Nuclear > Wind keeps thermal and hydro on top (now: Thermal > Solar > Wind > Hydro > Nuclear).

s:
Match
List-I with
List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists: List- I List- II (States) (Rank in installed thermal power capacity)
A. Gujarat
1. First
B. Maharashtra
2. Second
C. Uttar Pradesh
3. Third
D. West Bengal
4. Fourth A B C D
x: The options give all-India thermal plant load factor: in the mid-2000s the average PLF was about 70-75%. The match list in the stem does not fit these options.

s: Which one of the following states of India ranks first in installed capacity and generation of electricity?
x:
in 2006 Maharashtra led in installed capacity and generation — now Gujarat is first (app notes 4:99, Dec 2025)
Gujarat is now first in gross installed capacity (Dec 2025) (in 2006 Maharashtra was first).

s: In the year 2006-2007, the share of nuclear energy generated in India in the total energy generated was –
x: In 2006-07 nuclear stations gave about 18.8 billion units, only about 2.8% of total generation, so 'less than 3 percent' is right; 3-4% fits the early 2000s.

s: Which among the following ranks first in wind power generation?
x: Gujarat is now first in wind power (Dec 2025), ahead of Tamil Nadu; among the options it also led Maharashtra, Karnataka and Rajasthan in 2013.

s:
With reference to coal-based thermal power plants in India, consider the following statements:
1. None of them uses seawater.
2. None of them is set up in water-stressed district.
3. None of them is privately owned.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Some coal plants use seawater, some are in water-stressed districts and many are private, so none of the statements is correct.

s: Fly ash pollution is caused by
x: Fly ash is the by-product of burning coal in thermal power plants.

s: With the help of which of the following countries, Thermal Power Centre at Obra was established?
x: Obra thermal power station (Sonbhadra, UP) was built with Russian (Soviet) help.

s:
Match
List-I with
List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below : List -I
List-II (Coal Based Power Plant) (Located in State)
A. Kahalgaon
1. Madhya Pradesh
B. Khargone
2. Bihar
C. Korba

x: Kahalgaon–Bihar, Khargone–MP, Korba–Chhattisgarh, Kudgi–Karnataka: A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3.

s: The thermal power plant of Bokaro is located in :
x: Bokaro Thermal Power Station is in Jharkhand.

s: Uran is a gas-based power project in –
x: Uran gas turbine power station is in Raigad, Maharashtra.

s: The Barh Super Thermal Power Station (BSTPS) is located in which State?
x: Barh Super Thermal Power Station is in Patna district, Bihar.

s:
Match the following Coal-based Thermal Power Stations and their States:
List I -
List II

a. Kudgi -
I. Chhattisgarh

b. Kahalgaon -
II. Karnataka

c. Sipat -
III. U.P.

d. Dadri -
IV. Bihar
x: Kudgi–Karnataka, Kahalgaon–Bihar, Sipat–Chhattisgarh, Dadri–UP: a-II, b-IV, c-I, d-III.

s: Which of the following is currently the biggest Thermal Power Plant (with an installed capacity of 4,760 MW) in India?
o: Vindhyachal Thermal Power Station, Madhya Pradesh
Rihand Thermal Power Station, Uttar Pradesh
Talcher Super Thermal Power Station, Odisha Answer: (B) Vindhyachal Thermal Power Station, Madhya Pradesh
x: Vindhyachal (NTPC, Singrauli, MP; 4,760 MW) is India's biggest thermal plant; Mundra is second (4,620 MW).

s: Ramagundam Super Thermal Power Station is located in–
x:
Telangana was carved out of Andhra Pradesh on 2 June 2014 — now Ramagundam is in Telangana (AP Reorganisation Act 2014)
NTPC's Ramagundam STPS (2,600 MW) is in Peddapalli district, which was in Andhra Pradesh when asked (now Telangana).

src: APPSC Dental Asst. Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Officers,
s: As per Sustainable energy for All Report, 2015, how many people in the World live without electricity?
x: The Sustainable Energy for All Global Tracking Framework 2015 counted about 1.1 billion people without electricity. 0.9 billion and 1 billion are later or rounded figures.

src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
s: What rank in the world of Indian in terms of number of dams?
x: India ranks 3rd in the number of large dams, after China and the USA.

s: Which is the first hydel power plant in India?
x: India's first hydel station was Sidrapong, Darjeeling (1897); Sivasamudram came in 1902.

s: In which one of the following states is Siul river project located?
x: Baira Siul project is on the Siul (a Ravi tributary) in Chamba, Himachal Pradesh.

s: Which of the following is related to the field of electricity generation?
x: NHPC is a hydro-power generation company; MMTC is trade, MTNL telecom, NCL coal.

s: Which hydropower plant in Bhutan was inaugurated recently by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi?
x: PM Modi inaugurated the Mangdechhu hydropower plant in Bhutan in 2019.

s: Singrauli Small Hydro Power Project is located in–
x: The Singrauli small hydro project (2 x 4 MW) is in Sonbhadra, Uttar Pradesh.

s:
Which of the following pairs are correctly matched?
1. Idukki : Thermal power station
2. Sabarigiri : Hydro - electric project
3. Ghatprabha : Irrigation Project
4. Ramganga : Multipurpose project
x: Idukki is a hydel (not thermal) project; Sabarigiri hydel, Ghatprabha irrigation and Ramganga multipurpose are right, so 2, 3 and 4.

s: Shiva Samundram Hydropower Project is located in-
x: Shivasamudram is on the Kaveri in Karnataka.

s: Salal Hydroelectric Project is situated in
x: Salal project is on the Chenab in Reasi, Jammu and Kashmir.

s: The first hydro power project developed in India is
x: Sidrapong (Darjeeling, 1897) was first but is not offered; of the options Shivanasamudra (1902) is the oldest.

s: The first hydroelectricity plant was developed in India at
x: India's first hydroelectric plant was at Sidrapong, Darjeeling (1897).

s: Which Hydropower plant in Bhutan was inaugrated recently by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi?
x: PM Modi inaugurated the Mangdechhu hydropower plant in Bhutan in 2019.

s: Which of the following is the oldest Hydropower Station in India?
x: Shivasamudram (1902) is older than Pallivasal, Machkund and Mayurakshi.

s: There are huge possibilities of hydroelectricity in the Himalayan region. 2. Eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar cannot utilise this potential because the Himalayas situated to their North lies in boundary of Nepal. Select the correct answer from the code given below :
x: Statement 1 is right (snow-fed Himalayan rivers have huge hydel potential); statement 2 is taken as wrong per the key – eastern UP and Bihar can use it through India-Nepal projects (Kosi, Gandak).

src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
s: Kerosene oil floats on water because
at: Its density is less than the density of water
x: Kerosene floats because its density is less than that of water and it does not mix with water.

src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
s: Cooking gas (LPG) is?
x: LPG is a liquefied mixture of propane and butane; it is not one gas alone.

src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
s: Which of the following is obtained at lowest temperature by fractional distillation of petroleum?
x: In fractional distillation the lightest fraction, gasoline (petrol, C5-C10), separates at the lowest temperature, before kerosene, diesel and heavy oil.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
s: Among the following fuels, the one with the highest calorific value is
x: Natural gas (methane, about 50,000 kJ/kg) has a higher calorific value than diesel (about 45,000), brown coal and wood.

src: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022
s: Bio-Gas mainly consists of
x: Biogas is mainly methane (50-75%) with CO2.

s:
Match List‑I (Fuel Gases) with List‑II (Major Constituents) and select the correct answer using the codes given below the Lists: List‑I (Fuel Gases)
A. CNG
B. Coal gas
C. LPG
D. Water gas List‑II (Major Constituents)
1. Carbon monoxide, Hydrogen
2. Butane, Propane
3. Methane, Ethane
4. Hydrogen, Methane, Carbon monoxide
Codes:
x: CNG is methane and ethane (A-3), coal gas is hydrogen, methane and CO (B-4), LPG is butane and propane (C-2), water gas is CO and hydrogen (D-1).

s: The major component of CNG is:
x: CNG is compressed natural gas, mainly methane (CH4).

s: Which of the following is the main component of natural gas?
x: Natural gas consists mainly of methane, with some ethane, propane and butane.

s: Which one of the following can provide both power and manure?
x: A biogas plant gives fuel gas for power and the digested slurry as manure.

s: Which one of the following is called ‘syngas’?
x: Syngas (synthesis gas) is CO + H2, the same mixture as water gas.

s: Dihydrogen can be prepared on a commercial scale by the action of steam on hydrocarbons, when a mixture of CO and H 2 gas is formed. It is known as
x: Steam on hydrocarbons or coke gives CO + H2, called water gas (also syngas); producer gas contains nitrogen as well.

s: ______ was the first person to isolate methane gas. He discovered that methane mixture with air could be exploded using an electric spark.
x: Alessandro Volta isolated methane (marsh gas) in 1776 and showed that a methane-air mixture explodes with an electric spark.

s:
Match
List I with

List I
List II

1. CO + H2

B. Coal gas
2. CO + N2

C. Producer gas
3. CH4

x: Gobar gas is CH4 (A-3), coal gas is H2 + CH4 + CO (B-4), producer gas is CO + N2 (C-2), water gas is CO + H2 (D-1).

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
s: Which of the following emits higher quantity of Carbon Dioxide in terms of Kg CO2 per kWh?
x: Anthracite emits about 0.37 kg CO2 per kWh, slightly more than house coal (0.35) and far more than LPG (about 0.23); wood logs are counted nearly carbon-neutral.

s: Which among the following has the world's largest reserves of uranium?
x: Australia has the largest uranium resources (28%), ahead of Kazakhstan and Canada.

s: Which of the following places does not have heavywater plant for atomic energy?
x: Kalpakkam has an atomic power station but no heavy-water plant; Hazira, Thal and Tuticorin have heavy-water plants.

s: Anushakti Vidyut Nigam Limited is a joint venture of the Nuclear Power Corporation of India and
x: Anushakti Vidyut Nigam is a JV of NPCIL (51%) and NTPC (49%).

s: The first nuclear reactor of India is named –
x: Apsara (August 1956, Trombay) was India's first nuclear reactor.

s: Russia has agreed to install how many units of nuclear reactors in Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant?
x: Russia agreed to build six units at Kudankulam (two under the 1988 agreement, four more later).

s: In which place was the first Nuclear Power Station established in India?
x: Tarapur (Maharashtra, 1969) was India's first nuclear power station.

s: Where was the first nuclear power station established in the world?
x:
Most books and keys: USA (EBR-I, 1951). Strictly, Obninsk, USSR (1954) was the first grid-connected nuclear power station and Calder Hall, UK (1956) the first commercial-scale one.
The USA's EBR-I (1951) first produced nuclear electricity, so the key is USA.

s: Which of the following pairs related to States of India and proposed nuclear power plants is not correctly matched?

s: Which of the following countries is the largest reservoir of coal?

Most books and keys: China. Strictly, BP/EI proved-reserve data since about 2018 put Australia (14%) just ahead of China (13%) (PMF Human & Economic Geography 03 p.18); China led when the question was set (2010).
Of the options, China has the larger coal reserves (Australia is close and by some 2020s counts slightly ahead); New Zealand and Brazil are minor.

s:
In India, what is the role of the Coal Controller's Organization (CCO)?
1. CCO is the major source of Coal Statistics in Government of India.
2. It monitors progress of development of Captive Coal/Lignite blocks.
3. It hears any objection to the Government's notification relating to acquisition of coal-bearing areas.
4. It ensures that coal mining companies deliver the coal to end users in the prescribed time.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: The Coal Controller's Organisation is the main source of coal statistics, monitors captive coal/lignite blocks and hears objections to acquisition of coal-bearing areas; it does not enforce delivery times (statement 4).

s: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of proved coal reserves in the Indian States in decreasing order?
x:
Key / most books: Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, WB (proved). By total resources Odisha (94.5 bn t) now leads Jharkhand (87.8) (Ministry of Coal, 1.4.2023).
By proved (measured) reserves: Jharkhand (55.7 bn t) > Odisha (52.0) > Chhattisgarh (37.2) > West Bengal.

s: The biggest reserve of coal is found in
x:
Most books and keys: Jharkhand. By total resources Odisha is now first (94.5 vs 87.8 bn t, Ministry of Coal 1.4.2023; PMF Human & Economic Geography 03 p.22).
Jharkhand has the largest proved coal reserves (55.7 bn t measured, 1.4.2023).

s:
Consider the following statements with reference to coal :

Select the correct answer from the code given below:
x: India is the world's second-largest coal producer, and Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh have vast reserves, so both statements are correct.

s: Which of the following countries is the leading country in the reserve of Hard Coal?
x: Among the options China has by far the largest hard-coal reserves; India's are smaller and Nepal and New Zealand have little.

s: Which state in India produces the largest amount of coal ?
x: Of the options Orissa (Odisha) was the largest coal producer (Talcher, Ib valley), ahead of Madhya Pradesh; West Bengal's output is small and Bihar's coalfields went to Jharkhand in 2000.

src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding coal mining in India?

(I) Since March 1960, SCCL is a joint undertaking of the Government of Assam and the Government of India, sharing its equity in a 45 : 55 ratio.

(II) In 1973, the various privately owned coal mines at Raniganj were nationalised.

(III) National Coal Development Corporation Ltd. (NCDC) was set up in 1956.
x: (I) is wrong – SCCL is a Government of Telangana–Government of India company sharing equity 51:49, not Assam 45:55. (II) is right – non-coking coal mines incl. Raniganj were nationalised in 1973. (III) is right – NCDC was set up in 1956. So II and III.

s: For which one of the following Satara is well known ?
x:
Official key / most books: Wind Energy Plant (Chalkewadi). Strictly, the Koyna hydro-electric project is also in Satara district, so 'Hydro-Electric Plant' is defensible (Maharashtra power-station lists).
Satara district (Maharashtra) is known for its wind farms – Chalkewadi and Vankusawade on the Sahyadri plateau; thermal and nuclear plants are not located there.

s: Which one of the following states is a leading producer of Solar energy in India?
x:
Karnataka led installed solar capacity till 2021 — now Rajasthan is 1st in installed solar (pv-magazine India, Sep 2021; MNRE state-wise data)
In 2020 Karnataka (Pavagada park) had the largest installed solar capacity, about 7.4 GW, ahead of Rajasthan (5.2 GW) (now Rajasthan leads, since Sept 2021).

s: For which one of the following, is Satara well known?
x:

Satara district (Maharashtra) is known for its wind farms – Chalkewadi and Vankusawade on the Sahyadri plateau; thermal and nuclear plants are not located there.

s: Which state has the highest potential for the development of solar energy?
x: By the NISE/MNRE assessment Rajasthan has the highest solar potential, about 142 GW of the national 749 GW (J&K about 111 GW next); MP, UP and Jharkhand are far lower.

s: Rampura, which became the first village in India to have its solar power plant, is situated in –
x: Rampura village in Jhansi district, Uttar Pradesh, runs on a community solar power plant (about 9 kW) set up with an NGO and is cited as India's first solar-powered village.

s: Which of the following states of India have the higher opportunities for the development of wind power?
x: Tamil Nadu and Gujarat are the leading wind States in both potential and installed capacity (Gujarat 1st, TN 2nd, Dec 2025); UP, Punjab, Bihar, Jharkhand and Odisha have low wind potential.

s: The biggest wind energy project in Asia with a capacity of 150 megawatts is located in :
x: Muppandal (Kanyakumari, Tamil Nadu) was Asia's biggest wind-farm cluster at the time (150 MW); Gujarat, Maharashtra and Karnataka had smaller farms then.

s: Which of the following stations is not on the Trans-Siberian railway in Russia?
x: Leningrad (St. Petersburg), Moscow and Vladivostok are all on the Trans-Siberian route; Georgia is a separate country in the Caucasus, not a station.

s: Trans-Siberian Railway runs between the stations in Russia from:
x: The Trans-Siberian main line runs from Moscow to Vladivostok (9,289 km, 8 time zones). NCERT and PMF trace the route from St. Petersburg, but the railway itself is the Moscow-Vladivostok line; Khabarovsk is only an intermediate city.

s: Euro tunnel for fast running trains joins :
x: The Channel Tunnel (Eurotunnel) runs under the English Channel and links England (UK) with France (London-Paris); Holland, Belgium and Luxembourg are not its ends.

s: The Canadian Pacific Railway runs between –
x: The Canadian Pacific, Canada's first transcontinental line (1885), runs from Montreal to Vancouver. Halifax-Vancouver is how NCERT describes the 'Trans-Canadian' line, so it is the tempting wrong option for the CPR.

s: Transcanadian Highway connects
x: The Trans-Canada Highway links Vancouver (British Columbia, west coast) with St. John's in Newfoundland (east coast), which the option calls 'Saint John City'. Montreal, Toronto and Quebec are only on the way.

s: The longest continental railway in the world is
x: The Trans-Siberian (Moscow-Vladivostok, 9,289 km) is the longest continuous railway in the world; the Canadian National and Canadian Pacific lines are much shorter, and there is no 'Transatlantic Railway'.

s: Which one of the following trains/railways passes through Germany, France, Austria, Hungary and Romania?
x: The Orient Express (Paris-Istanbul) ran across France, Germany, Austria, Hungary and Romania; the Trans-Siberian is in Russia, the Cape-Cairo line in Africa and the Union/Central Pacific in the USA.

x:
Official key: USA, Canada, India, Germany (older data). Strictly now: USA, India, Canada, Germany (Rocket World Geography #17 p.27).

The UPPSC key is USA, Canada, India, Germany (option 3), from older data that put Canada's network ahead of India's. Current figures are USA (~220,000 km) > India (~69,000-70,000 km) > Canada (~49,000 km) > Germany (~33,000-39,800 km), an order no option shows (now USA > India > Canada > Germany).

s: The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana is :
o: To augment road connectivity and provide food grains
To facilitate patrolling of the area to prevent misuse
To help police to reach the place of crime more swiftly
To develop community life in villages which are not
x: PMGSY (25 December 2000) is a rural roads scheme giving all-weather road connectivity to unconnected habitations, so the road-connectivity option is the answer; patrolling, crime response and 'community life' are not its aim. (The 'food grains' wording is the printed option's, not part of PMGSY.)

s: The east-west corridor national highway connects which of the following?
x: The East-West Corridor runs from Silchar (Assam) to Porbandar (Gujarat) and meets the North-South Corridor at Jhansi; it is not Dibrugarh-Surat or any of the other pairs.

s: Which state has maximum road density?
x: Kerala has India's highest road density (6,690.30 km per 1,000 sq km on 31 March 2019; 517.77 per 100 sq km in NCERT's 2011 data), far above Punjab (2,935.98), Gujarat and Haryana.

s: In September 2022, NITI Aayog and World Resources Institute (WRI), launched India's first National Electric Freight Platform- E-FAST India. The full form of E-FAST is:

Electric Freight Accumulator for Sustainable Transport

x: e-FAST India, launched by NITI Aayog with WRI India in 2022, is the Electric Freight Accelerator for Sustainable Transport; the other options change 'Freight', 'Accelerator' or 'Sustainable'.

s: What is the rank of Andhra Pradesh in terms of length of coast line amongst the coastal states of India?
x:
the old count gave AP 974 km and 2nd place (printed key 'Second') — now 3rd with 1,053.07 km after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu 1,068.69 km (PIB Release 2198800, 4 Dec 2025)
In the revised coastline count (India 11,098.81 km) Andhra Pradesh has 1,053.07 km and ranks third, after Gujarat (2,340.62 km) and Tamil Nadu (1,068.69 km) (now 3rd; it was '2nd, 974 km' when this 2023 paper was set).
